outcome: subjective birth experience (emotional experience, participation, professional support, coping possibilities, global birth judgement)
psychological distress symptoms (postpartum depression, impact of event scale)
cohort: 307 first-time mothers who planned to give birth vaginally.
finding: Prepartum fear of childbirth significantly affects all dimensions of the subjective birth experience up to six months postpartum, correlating with maternal mental health.
mod_finding: Mode of birth influenced the dimensions of participation and global birth judgment, and showed a complex interplay with fear of birth and time for emotional experience.
